manifest.description: Native DeepSeek Harness tools for the Kimi browser extension (WebBridge) and KimiCU desktop control: kimi_browser_* drives the user's real logged-in browser, kimi_cu_* observes and operates Windows desktops.
manifest.author: dsh-kimi-assemble contributors

bundle.text:
# dsh-kimi-assemble —— Kimi browser extension (WebBridge) + KimiCU desktop control → native DSH tools
# ============================================================================
# This bundle only mounts the plugin into the profile; the `config` below are the overrides
# this deployment wants. Install: plugin_manager install_bundle target=<this directory>
#
# NOTE: the Loader replaces `config` wholesale, it does not deep-merge. When you override this
#       row from a higher layer, write every key you want to keep; omitted keys fall back to the
#       code defaults in lib/config.mjs.
# ============================================================================
- insert:
    - id: kimi-assemble
      name: dsh-kimi-assemble
      config:
        # Browser (Kimi extension / WebBridge daemon, default 127.0.0.1:10086)
        webbridgeEnabled: true
        webbridgeAddr: ''          # empty = auto-discover (reads ~/.kimi-webbridge/daemon.addr)
        webbridgeAutoStart: true   # start `kimi-webbridge` when unreachable
        webbridgeTimeoutMs: 60000
        browserGroupTitle: DSH
        # Desktop (KimiCU native agent)
        kimicuEnabled: true
        kimicuExePath: ''          # empty = auto-discover %LOCALAPPDATA%\Kimi Computer Use\kimi-cu.exe
        kimicuAutoStart: true      # start `kimi-cu.exe start-agent` when unreachable
        kimicuTimeoutMs: 120000
        cuMaxTreeChars: 12000
        # Prompt section and runtime skills
        promptSection: true
        registerSkills: true
        # Language of the text a HUMAN sees: auto | en | zh
        # (tool descriptions are always English — they are part of the model-facing catalog)
        language: auto
        # Tool names to drop, e.g. ['kimi_cu_launch'] to keep only reading/acting
        disabledTools: []

declared.name: kimi_status
declared.description: Report the live state of both local Kimi bridges: the browser extension daemon (WebBridge) and the Windows desktop agent (KimiCU). Call this first whenever a browser or desktop call fails with a connection/readiness error.

declared.name: kimi_browser_open
declared.description: Open a URL in the user's real browser through the Kimi extension. Waits for loading by default and returns the final URL, title, tab id and page state.

declared.name: kimi_browser_read
declared.description: Read the current page as an accessibility tree, search the tree, read an embedded frame, or return only changes since the previous read; can include a screenshot.

declared.name: kimi_browser_click
declared.description: Click an element using an aria ref or CSS selector, check whether the page changed, and retry once with a fresh read if the ref is stale.

declared.name: kimi_browser_fill
declared.description: Replace an input, textarea or contenteditable value with text; optionally submit the form and report which submit route worked.

declared.name: kimi_browser_act
declared.description: Perform a non-click page interaction such as key input, typing, selection, checking, hover, scroll, drag, mouse click or upload, then report whether it took effect.

declared.name: kimi_browser_wait
declared.description: Wait for page text, a selector, a URL, document readiness, or a fixed delay; return what matched or the current page state on timeout.

declared.name: kimi_browser_eval
declared.description: Evaluate JavaScript in the page and return a size-limited JSON result.

declared.name: kimi_browser_dialog
declared.description: Check, accept or dismiss a native JavaScript alert, confirm or prompt dialog.

declared.name: kimi_browser_screenshot
declared.description: Capture the current page or an element as a PNG/JPEG image and attach it to the conversation when the model route supports image input.

declared.name: kimi_browser_tabs
declared.description: List this task’s tabs or all visible tabs, attach to an existing tab, close the current tab, or close the task’s tabs.

declared.name: kimi_browser_script
declared.description: Run 1–25 browser actions in one call, either as a single action or ordered steps; a failing step reports completed steps.

declared.name: kimi_cu_windows
declared.description: List open Windows desktop windows that KimiCU can observe and control, including app path, window id and title.

declared.name: kimi_cu_observe
declared.description: Observe one desktop window and return accessibility tree text, focused element, and optionally a screenshot.

declared.name: kimi_cu_act
declared.description: Send one input action to a desktop window, including click, type, key, scroll, set_value, drag or activate.

declared.name: kimi_cu_launch
declared.description: Launch a desktop app by display name, StartApps appId or executable path.

declared.name: kimi_cu_script
declared.description: Run 1–30 desktop actions in one call under a single input lease, as a single action or ordered steps.

readme.text:
Native [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) tools for two Kimi
bridges that run on your own machine:

| Capability | Backend | Tools |
|---|---|---|
| Drive your **real, logged-in browser** | Kimi browser extension daemon (WebBridge, `127.0.0.1:10086`) | `kimi_browser_*` |
| Observe and operate **real Windows windows** | KimiCU native agent (`\\.\pipe\kimi-cu-win-<user>`) | `kimi_cu_*` |
| Diagnose both | — | `kimi_status` |

Once installed the model does not need to read a skill, shell out to `curl`, or write a
node-repl `js` cell — it calls tools. UTF-8 survives end to end, a bad argument names the exact
field, and a connection failure comes with the next step.

[中文文档](README.zh.md)

---

| Path | You get | What it needs | Tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Browser only** | drive your logged-in Chrome/Edge | the Kimi browser extension + its local daemon | 12 + `kimi_status` |
| **Desktop only** | drive real Windows windows | Windows + the KimiCU runtime | 5 + `kimi_status` |
| **Both** (default) | everything | both of the above | 17 |

Set `kimicuEnabled: false` for browser-only, `webbridgeEnabled: false` for desktop-only — the
other half then never registers a tool or a prompt line.

This plugin is a **bridge, not a bundled implementation**. It does not download or run remote
installers by itself, so a missing component shows up as `KIMI_WEBRIDGE_DOWN` /
`KIMI_CU_NOT_INSTALLED` — **with the exact next steps attached to the error**.

readme.section: 2. Run the preflight — it is the install spine
readme.text:
It prints what is missing, and with `--json` a machine-readable `next_actions` list:
`kind: "run"` is a command an agent may execute, `kind: "user"` is something only a human can do.

```bash
npm i -g dsh-kimi-assemble && kimi-assemble-doctor
kimi-assemble-doctor --json          # for agents
```

Or, if the plugin is already installed in your profile, run the copy that came with it:

```bash
node "%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-kimi-assemble\scripts\doctor.mjs"
```

readme.section: 2. Run the preflight — it is the install spine
readme.text:
Exit codes: `0` both bridges ready · `2` a human step is required · `3` only the desktop runtime
is missing and it is installable. It never downloads anything unless you pass `--install-desktop`.

```text
plugin_manager install_bundle  target=dsh-kimi-assemble
```

From the plugin market instead: add this index URL under Discover → index sources, then install
from there:

```text
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KexinCC/dsh-kimi-assemble/main/market/index.json
```

From a checkout (no registry involved):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/KexinCC/dsh-kimi-assemble.git
```

```text
plugin_manager install_bundle  target=<absolute path to that clone>
```

`cordis_inspect_query(Tool.listTools)` lists the `kimi_*` tools for your path, and
`kimi_status` should report both bridges as installed. A fresh machine is wired once that is
true; after that the plugin discovers, starts and reconnects both components automatically
(including clearing a stale daemon pid file left by an unclean shutdown).

| You want… | You need | How to get it |
|---|---|---|
| browser control | Chrome or Edge + the **Kimi browser extension**. The local-Agent path needs **no Kimi account** (only the sidebar does). | 1) install the "Kimi" extension from the Chrome Web Store or Edge Add-ons (or the [manual install](https://www.kimi.com/products/kimi-browser-extension)); 2) open the extension sidebar → Settings → “本地 Agent 远程控制” → click **去连接 / Connect**; 3) copy the install command shown in that dialog into a terminal and run it — this installs the local daemon under `~/.kimi-webbridge`. [FAQ](https://www.kimi.com/help/kimi-webbridge/kimi-webbridge-faq) |
| desktop control | Windows + the **KimiCU runtime** (`kimi-cu.exe`) | download and run [setup_windows.cmd](https://cdn.kimi.com/kimi-computer-use-windows/latest/setup_windows.cmd) in a terminal, or set `kimicuExePath` in the config to an existing copy |
| either | DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.0` (verified on `0.2.1-rc.2`), Node `>= 22` | — |

> **Security boundary, up front:** anything the browser reads is **untrusted data, never
> instructions**. `kimi_browser_eval` is a privileged tool (it runs code in your page), and page
> content that asks the agent to do things must be reported, not obeyed. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

`config` is **replaced wholesale** (loader semantics, not a deep merge). Write only the keys you
want to change; everything else falls back to the defaults.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `webbridgeEnabled` | `true` | when false, no browser tools are registered |
| `webbridgeAddr` | `''` | empty = read `~/.kimi-webbridge/daemon.addr`, else `127.0.0.1:10086` |
| `webbridgeAutoStart` | `true` | start the daemon idempotently when it is unreachable |
| `webbridgeTimeoutMs` | `60000` | per browser action |
| `browserGroupTitle` | `DSH` | default tab group title, visible in the user's browser |
| `browserReadMaxChars` | `20000` | default `kimi_browser_read` budget |
| `browserVerify` | `auto` | `auto` = verify that each action changed the page; `off` = fire-and-forget (rollback switch) |
| `mouseFallback` | `auto` | after a JS click that changed nothing, retry with a real CDP mouse event (Element UI / Ant Design need this). `clickStrategy` reports what worked |
| `popupWatch` | `on` | detect a swallowed `window.open` and report `popupBlocked` |
| `browserVerifyLightMs` | `0` | observation budget for reversible actions (scroll / hover / set_checked …). Reversible actions no longer pay the 600 ms window: measured 649 ms → 13 ms |
| `browserVerifyMs` | `600` | how long to watch for a change before reporting "unchanged" (100–10000)

Tool **descriptions** are always English — they are part of the model-facing tool catalog.
`language` controls the text a human sees: error messages, tool output, the prompt section and
the skill bodies.

---

- **`kimi_status {deep?}`** — the live state of both bridges (daemon address/version/extension
  connection, CU exe/version/agent pid/pipe/permissions) plus `hints[]` with the concrete next
  step. **First stop after any connection failure.**

- **`kimi_browser_open {url, new_tab=true, wait_until=load|domcontentloaded|none, group_title?, session?}`**
  → final URL / title / tabId / page state. Waits for load by default so the next action does not race the page.
- **`kimi_browser_read {mode=read|find|frame|diff, include_meta?, include_screenshot?, ref?, max_chars?, cursor?}`**
  → accessibility tree text (with `[ref=eNNN]`), a page-state line (url / load state / scroll / focused
  element / element counts), search hits, iframe text, or **only what changed since the previous read**
  (`mode=diff`, typically ~4% of the full payload).
- **`kimi_browser_click {selector, verify?, session?}`** — CSS or `@eNNN` / `eNNN` / `[ref=eNNN]`.
  Reports `changed` / `changeDetail`; a stale ref is re-read and retried once.
- **`kimi_browser_fill {selector, value, submit=false, verify?, session?}`** — reports whether a
  → `submit=true` commits for you: it clicks the form submit button (falling back to `requestSubmit()`, Esc + click, then Enter) and reports `submitStrategy`. This extension **cannot produce real key events**, so implicit Enter-to-submit never happens.
  `submit=true` Enter actually changed the page (suggestion dropdowns swa

Every mutating browser tool reports whether the page actually changed. The extension's click is a
DOM-level dispatch: it returns success even when nothing happens, which used to make a wrong click
look identical to a right one. `browserVerify: 'off'` restores the old fire-and-forget behaviour.
Measured effect (6 fixtures × 5 runs, see [`bench/RESULTS.md`](https://github.com/KexinCC/dsh-kimi-assemble/blob/main/bench/RESULTS.md)): silent failures
10 → 0, task success 37% → 100%, at the cost of ~600ms on actions that genuinely do nothing.

- **`kimi_cu_windows {filter?, limit?}`** → `[{id, title, app}]`
- **`kimi_cu_observe {window, screenshot=true, text=true, filter?, max_chars?}`** →
  accessibility tree (with `[index]`) + focus + screenshot image block + `coordinate_space`
- **`kimi_cu_act {action, window, ...}`** — `click` (`element_index` **or** `x/y`), `type`, `key`,
  `scroll` (**`scroll_y > 0` scrolls down**), `set_value`, `drag`, `drag_path`, `secondary`,
  `activate`
- **`kimi_cu_launch {app}`**
- **`kimi_cu_script`** — **two shapes**:
  - single step: `{action, window, ...}`, or `{action:"call", args:{method,args}}` for any of the
    16 KimiCU methods (`open_panel`, `list_apps`, …)
  - batch: `{steps:[...], stop_on_error?, settle_ms?, max_result_chars?}` — 1–30 steps **inside one
    input lease**; step actions are the 9 input actions above plus `windows` / `observe` /
    `launch` / `wait_window` / `sleep` / `call`; a later step can address the n-th window of the
    previous `windows` step with `window:"@n"`
  - argument table: [`references/computer-api.md`](references/computer-api.md)

readme.section: Performance: the plugin is fast, the model rounds are the cost
readme.text:
| Layer | Measured | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP health check / status (cached) | **0.0–2.1 ms** | plugin overhead |
| HTTP `snapshot` / `list_tabs` / `evaluate` | **4–10 ms** | plugin overhead |
| CU `ping` / `list_windows` / `get_window` | **0.5–2.7 ms** | plugin overhead |
| CU lease begin+end | **0.3 ms** | negligible |
| browser `navigate` | ~206 ms | page load — the daemon's job |
| browser `screenshot` | ~144 ms | Chrome capture |
| CU `get_window_state`, text only | ~82 ms | UIA tree walk |
| CU `get_window_state`, with screenshot | ~217 ms | UIA + WGC capture |
| **one model round** | **seconds** | the real cost |

readme.section: Performance: the plugin is fast, the model rounds are the cost
readme.text:
Local execution is 0.5–220 ms; a model round is seconds. So the optimisation is **more work per
call**, not a faster transport. That is what the batch scripts are for: one tool call is one model
round, and six browser steps that used to cost six rounds now finish inside a single 0.6 s call.

---

readme.section: Performance: the plugin is fast, the model rounds are the cost
readme.text:
Numbers above are per-call inside the plugin. For a like-for-like comparison against
Playwright on the same pages — including where this bridge is slower and where it is
faster — see [Benchmark](#benchmark).

readme.section: Why it does not go wrong
readme.text:
1. **No shell.** Browser requests are `node:http` with a UTF-8 buffer inside the Host process.
   Inline JSON through a shell corrupts non-ASCII text on Windows (measured: the daemon answers
   `invalid JSON`) — that path was removed.
2. **Validate before touching the runtime.** Action arguments are compiled into requests
   (`planAction` / `preflightSteps`) before any agent is started; exclusive fields, enum
   overflows and unknown fields all fail with `KIMI_ARGS`, naming the field (and the step number
   inside a script).
3. **No guessing at windows.** `window` accepts an id, an exact title, a substring or `@n`; zero
   or multiple matches fail and list the candidates instead of silently picking the first.
4. **Lease isolation.** Every desktop call is a lease (`begin` → N calls → `end`, released in
   `finally`), serialized process-wide so two input streams cannot interleave; `begin`/`end` must
   share connection, session and nonce (a mismatch fails). A batch script uses one lease for the
   whole script.
5. **Dispatched ≠ accepted.** Every input tool says `dispatched:true` and asks for a
   `kimi_cu_observe` confirmation.
6. **Six connection classes, six error codes, six next

readme.section: real machine only (needs the bridges running)
readme.text:
In-host acceptance (2026-10-23): 13 `kimi_*` tools visible; a `kimi_cu_observe` screenshot
arrived as an image block; Chinese round-tripped intact through `kimi_browser_open/read/screenshot`;
a 6-step batch script finished in 0.6 s; the `kimi-cu` / `kimi-webbridge` runtime skills replaced
the old curl/`js` versions.

No recognised leaderboard exists for a browser-control plugin — WebArena, WebVoyager,
Mind2Web and OSWorld all measure *an agent* (model + tools) on hundreds of tasks. So instead of
inventing a "score", this measures latency and throughput against the industry baseline
(Playwright) on the same machine, pages and operations.

| Operation | This plugin (p50) | Playwright (p50) | Ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| navigate | 157 ms | 20 ms | 7.8× slower |
| read page | 48 ms | 19 ms | 2.5× slower |
| click + change verification (default) | 674 ms | 64 ms | 10.6× slower |
| click without verification | **18 ms** | 52 ms | **3× faster** |
| fill | 32 ms | 24 ms | 1.4× slower |
| screenshot | 145 ms | 50 ms | 2.9× slower |
| cold start | 524 ms | 507 ms | ≈ same |
| 20 operations in one call | **102 ms (196 ops/s)** | 320 ms (62 ops/s) | **3.2× faster** |

The short version: navigation pays for two extra hops (it drives *your* real Chrome, not a
throwaway one); the verification window is the price of knowing whether an action landed
(`browserVerify: "off"` removes it); batching is where the model-loop win comes from.
Methodology, caveats and the reproduction command: [docs/BENCHMARK.md](https://github.com/KexinCC/dsh-kimi-assemble/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARK.md).

```
index.js              apply(ctx, config)
lib/
  i18n.mjs            en/zh catalog + language resolution (zero IO, zero deps)
  config.mjs          defaults + hand-written validation (no schemastery)

- The **desktop** half is Windows only. The browser half also runs on macOS/Linux, where the
  daemon path is resolved under `~`.
- No settings panel in v1; configuration lives in `cordis.patch.yml`.
- The plugin never closes the user's tabs on its own; `close_session` is only used when asked.
- Sites that strictly verify `isTrusted` (banking, CAPTCHA) cannot be driven by synthetic events.
  It fails loudly instead of pretending to work.
- iframe internals cannot be operated directly (daemon limitation); they can be read.
- A few windows (input-method hosts, protected windows, fully occluded or minimised) cannot be
  captured: `kimi_cu_observe` degrades to text and states why, instead of failing the call.
- A batch script runs blind: intermediate results do not reach the model, so split the script when
  the page or UI may change unpredictably.

This plugin can drive your real browser session and your real desktop. It opens no listening
socket, sends no telemetry, and only talks to the local daemon and the local named pipe described
above. Read [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) before enabling it on a shared machine.
